title: A Survey on Recent Approaches for Natural Language Processing in Low-Resource Scenarios
summary: Surveys techniques for coping with scarce labeled data in NLP, organizing methods around data augmentation, distant supervision, and transfer learning, and discusses how their data requirements differ.

title: A Survey on Multilingual Large Language Models: Corpora, Alignment, and Bias
summary: Reviews multilingual LLM training corpora and cross-lingual representation alignment, arguing that under-representation of low-resource languages in training data continues to limit multilingual model quality.

title: Responsible Multilingual Large Language Models: A Survey of Development, Applications, and Societal Impact
summary: Reports that the large majority of the world's languages remain low-resource, and examines practical deployments of multilingual LLMs in customer service, search, and translation.

title: Exploring NLP Benchmarks in an Extremely Low-Resource Setting
summary: Studies machine translation into an extremely low-resource Romance language (Ladin), finding that LLM performance is biased toward high-resource languages even for linguistically related pairs.

title: Large Multimodal Models for Low-Resource Languages: A Survey
summary: Surveys multimodal (vision+language) modeling for low-resource languages, covering data creation, lightweight encoders, and cross-lingual transfer/adaptation techniques used to compensate for limited data.

title: FormosanBench: Benchmarking Low-Resource Austronesian Languages in the Era of Large Language Models
summary: Introduces a benchmark for extremely low-resource Austronesian languages, arguing that current LLM benchmarks systematically under-represent minority and endangered language families.

title: GlobalBench: A Benchmark for Global Progress in Natural Language Processing
summary: Proposes a benchmark tracking NLP progress across the world's languages, building on prior work documenting how few languages receive adequate NLP resourcing and evaluation coverage.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Natural Language Processing: A Survey
summary: Systematically reviews retrieval-augmented generation techniques, proposing a taxonomy of retrieval fusion strategies (query-based, logits-based, latent, parametric) and comparing them on accessibility and efficiency.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for AI-Generated Content: A Survey
summary: Reviews how retrieval augmentation is used across AI-generated content tasks beyond text, classifying approaches by how the retriever is coupled with the generator.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: One of the most cited RAG surveys; organizes RAG systems into Naive, Advanced, and Modular paradigms and examines the retrieval, generation, and augmentation components in turn.

title: Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
summary: Proposes a unified evaluation process for RAG systems and argues that hybrid retrieval+generation architectures make standard NLP evaluation metrics and benchmarks insufficient on their own.

title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey on Agentic RAG
summary: Argues that traditional RAG's static retrieve-then-generate workflow lacks the adaptability needed for multi-step reasoning, motivating agentic architectures with planning and iterative retrieval.

title: A Survey on Knowledge-Oriented Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Surveys RAG through the lens of structured and unstructured knowledge sources, discussing the difficulty of aligning retrieved knowledge with a generator's objectives.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Evaluation in the Era of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Compiles RAG-specific evaluation datasets and frameworks and performs a meta-analysis of evaluation practice, covering factual accuracy, safety, and computational efficiency.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
summary: Focuses on RAG robustness against noisy or adversarial retrieved context and lists open challenges including adaptive retrieval and multi-hop structured reasoning.

title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
summary: An early comprehensive hallucination survey proposing a taxonomy of hallucination types and reviewing detection/mitigation methods, including the limits of retrieval augmentation for factuality.

title: Large Language Models Hallucination: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: A later hallucination survey covering how hallucinations arise across generation tasks, with updated detection/mitigation taxonomies and a review of evaluation benchmarks and metrics.

title: Hallucination of Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Extends hallucination taxonomy and mitigation review to multimodal LLMs, covering vision-language-specific causes, benchmarks, and open challenges.

title: LLM-based Agents Suffer from Hallucinations: A Survey of Taxonomy, Methods, and Directions
summary: Analyzes hallucination specifically in LLM-based agents, decomposing agent behavior into internal belief state and external actions and cataloguing eighteen distinct triggering causes.

title: HalluciNot: Hallucination Detection Through Context and Common Knowledge Verification
summary: Proposes an enterprise hallucination-detection system (HDM-2) that separately validates model outputs against provided context versus general common knowledge, with word-level annotations.
